name: goth-atomic-provider-generation-replacement
instr:
Goth cannot rotate provider configuration atomically without disrupting authentication in progress. Implement generation-based replacement: active authentication keeps its provider, new authentication uses the latest generation, and retired generations remain available only to outstanding sessions. Without replacement, preserve registration, naming, redirects, provider deduction, callbacks, and logout.

Each replaceable provider must expose a deterministic, immutable session-compatibility identity covering all effective continuation settings. These include OAuth2 authorization, token, callback, scope, authentication-option, and provider-specific endpoints for GitHub, Google, Discord, and GitLab; issuer and discovery semantics for OpenID Connect; and team and endpoint semantics for Slack. Exclude client secrets, access tokens, runtime clients, debug settings, and ordinary authentication activity. GitHub, Google, Discord, GitLab, OpenID Connect, Slack, Twitter, and Steam must cover their OAuth2, OpenID, or OAuth1 continuation semantics without claiming unsupported refresh behavior.

`ReplaceProvider` atomically publishes exactly one generation only when registered and replacement names match and their identities are compatible under `ReplacementOptions`. Otherwise, `ReplacementError` leaves all visible provider and generation state unchanged; success returns a `ReplacementReceipt`. `AcquireProvider` and `AcquireProviderGeneration` return a `ProviderLease` for the exact instance
